findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax such as `HEAD; malicious-command`, `exec` runs the injected command with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` passed the branch literally; retain argument-vector execution rather than invoking a shell.

findings.title: [P2] Keep Git tied to the returned child process
findings.body:
On POSIX, `&` is valid in a Git branch name but is interpreted by the shell as a background operator. Calling `showBranch("topic&")` can make the shell exit before Git finishes, emit `exit` prematurely, and leave `child.kill()` unable to cancel the running Git descendant.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore argument-vector execution for branch names
findings.body:
`exec` runs the interpolated branch through a shell, enabling arbitrary command execution when `branch` is untrusted. For example, `showBranch("HEAD; malicious-command")` executes `malicious-command`; the previous `execFile` call passed the value as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch arguments out of the shell
findings.body:
On POSIX, valid branch names may contain shell metacharacters. Passing `$(yes>/dev/null)` causes an endless CPU-consuming command substitution before `git` starts; `exec`’s output limit cannot stop it because output is redirected. The previous `execFile` treated the branch literally.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
